tasks.gr12-civil-rights-movement-t2: Topic: Case study the US Civil Rights Movement for Grade 12 History (CAPS Topic 3). Cover the background of segregation, Brown v. Board of Education (1954), Martin Luther King Jr and the influence of Gandhi's passive resistance and civil disobedience, the Montgomery bus boycott (1955-56), Little Rock (1957), the Greensboro sit-ins (1960), Birmingham (1963), the March on Washington (28 August 1963), the Civil Rights Act (1964), Selma and the Voting Rights Act (1965), and the short- and long-term gains and limits. Ask factual, cause and source-skills questions.
tasks.gr12-black-power-movement-t2: Topic: Case study the Black Power Movement for Grade 12 History (CAPS Topic 3). Cover why Black Power arose (frustration after the Civil Rights Acts, the Watts uprising of 1965), Malcolm X and the Nation of Islam, Stokely Carmichael and SNCC, the slogan of June 1966, the Black Panther Party (Huey Newton and Bobby Seale, October 1966), its community programmes and the FBI's actions against it, how it differed from King's approach, and its gains and limits. Present different historians' judgements fairly. Ask factual, cause and source-skills questions.
tasks.gr12-women-and-peace-movements-t2: Topic: Women's liberation, women in South Africa and peace movements for Grade 12 History (CAPS Topic 3). Cover second-wave feminism (The Feminine Mystique of 1963, the National Organization for Women of 1966), South African women's resistance (FEDSAW of April 1954, the women's march to the Union Buildings on 9 August 1956, Lilian Ngoyi and Helen Joseph, the Black Sash of 1955, women in unions and the informal sector), and peace and anti-war movements (the Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament of 1958, the Vietnam Moratorium of 15 October 1969, Kent State in May 1970). Ask factual, cause and source-skills questions.
